category_title: Older adolescents with severe CHARGE syndrome and challenging behaviors
minimal_context: David is sitting in the classroom working on a table-top object sorting activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: David, it is time for your table-top activities. Here are the objects for sorting.

STUDENT: (David sits at the table but does not sort the objects, engaging in visual self-stimulatory behavior and teeth grinding instead.)

TUTOR: Look at the objects on the table. Put them in the right places.

STUDENT: (David pushes the sorting objects away, continuing to grind his teeth, and begins jumping up from his chair.)

TUTOR: Sit back down. You need to finish sorting these objects.

STUDENT: (David begins kicking and scratching to escape the activity.)

options.A: Undo his effort and show him the correct place for the object, then remove it and ask him to find the correct place.
options.B: Ask David where the object belongs, prompting: 'This one, you know it, you sorted it before.'
options.C: Terminate the task demands and remove the sorting materials from the table for 10 seconds.
options.D: Present the sorting objects within his intact visual field with good contrast and no visual clutter.
